title: FRITZ!Box
description: Every metric the FRITZ!Box 7590 AX delivers via fritz_exporter and fritz-extras. Provisioned from grafana/provisioning/dashboards/json/fritzbox.json.

panels.title: Firmware
panels.description: fritz_update_available. The label newsoftwareversion names the new version when one is available.

panels.title: Connection uptime
panels.description: Time since the last reconnect of the internet (PPP) connection.

panels.title: Last connection error
panels.description: last_error label of fritz_ppp_connection_state. ERROR_NONE = no error.

panels.title: Known devices
panels.description: All devices in the FRITZ!Box's device list, online or not.

panels.title: Phone numbers
panels.description: Telephone numbers configured on the FRITZ!Box.

panels.title: Download, 30 days
panels.description: Only counts what Prometheus has seen (data since 2026-10-10).

panels.title: Download bandwidth
panels.description: Yellow/red: actual traffic (fritz_wan_datarate_bytes). Green: current DSL sync rate, the real limit. Dashed: attainable rate of the line. Blue dots: speed tests (every 8 h).

panels.title: Upload bandwidth
panels.description: Yellow/red: actual traffic (fritz_wan_datarate_bytes). Green: current DSL sync rate, the real limit. Dashed: attainable rate of the line. Blue dots: speed tests (every 8 h).

panels.title: Daily traffic
panels.description: One bar per day, always the last 30 days (independent of the dashboard's time range). Each bar is the 24 h ending at its time stamp.

panels.title: Traffic compared: last 24 h, yesterday, a week ago
panels.description: Download + upload per hour. The other lines are the same hours one day and seven days earlier, drawn on top of the last 24 h. Legend 'Total' = traffic in those 24 h.

panels.title: Devices online now
panels.description: From the FRITZ!Box network list (Home Network → Network), read by fritz-extras every 5 min. Names are the ones set in the FRITZ!Box. DEVICE_ALLOWLIST in fritz.env limits which devices are named. Band and signal come from the FRITZ!Box Wi-Fi client list, matched by MAC; phones with private (random) MACs still match, as both sources see the same MAC.

targets.expr: max without () (max by (name, mac, interface, ip) (fritz_extras_host_info))

max without () (max by (name, mac, wifi_name) ((label_replace(fritz_wifi_client_signal_strength, "mac", "$1", "client_mac", "(.*)") * on (mac) group_left (name) max by (mac, name) (fritz_extras_host_info)) or on (mac) label_replace(label_replace(fritz_wifi_client_signal_strength, "mac", "$1", "client_mac", "(.*)"), "name", "$1", "client_ip", "(.*)")))

panels.title: Devices online by connection
panels.description: From the FRITZ!Box network list (Home Network → Network), read by fritz-extras every 5 min. Names are the ones set in the FRITZ!Box. DEVICE_ALLOWLIST in fritz.env limits which devices are named.

panels.title: Device online history
panels.description: From the FRITZ!Box network list (Home Network → Network), read by fritz-extras every 5 min. Names are the ones set in the FRITZ!Box. DEVICE_ALLOWLIST in fritz.env limits which devices are named. Green = online, grey = offline, empty = no data yet. Set the time range to 7 days to see daily patterns.

panels.title: Wi-Fi networks
panels.description: fritz_wifi_status, fritz_wifi_channel, fritz_wifi_associations_count per band.

panels.title: Client signal strength
panels.description: Device names come from fritz-extras, matched by MAC (IP if no name is known). The per-device table is under Devices.

targets.expr: max by (name, mac, wifi_name) ((label_replace(fritz_wifi_client_signal_strength, "mac", "$1", "client_mac", "(.*)") * on (mac) group_left (name) max by (mac, name) (fritz_extras_host_info)) or on (mac) label_replace(label_replace(fritz_wifi_client_signal_strength, "mac", "$1", "client_mac", "(.*)"), "name", "$1", "client_ip", "(.*)"))

panels.title: Client link speed
panels.description: Device names come from fritz-extras, matched by MAC (IP if no name is known). The per-device table is under Devices.

targets.expr: max by (name, mac, wifi_name) ((label_replace(fritz_wifi_client_speed, "mac", "$1", "client_mac", "(.*)") * on (mac) group_left (name) max by (mac, name) (fritz_extras_host_info)) or on (mac) label_replace(label_replace(fritz_wifi_client_speed, "mac", "$1", "client_mac", "(.*)"), "name", "$1", "client_ip", "(.*)"))

panels.title: Mesh link
panels.description: Backhaul path from the FRITZ!Box to the repeater, read by fritz-extras every 2 min from the mesh overview, including non-mesh hops such as powerline adapters. "direct": fritz_exporter's view, which only knows links between two mesh nodes (Wi-Fi backhaul or a plain cable), so it is empty while the repeater sits behind powerline.

panels.title: Mesh link rate
panels.description: The slowest hop of the backhaul path (the bottleneck), down = towards the repeater. Powerline: the PHY rate the adapters negotiated; real throughput is roughly half.

panels.title: Mesh link rate history
panels.description: Negotiated rate of each hop between the FRITZ!Box and the repeater (down = towards the repeater). LAN: the Ethernet port speed. Powerline: the adapters' PHY rate, which varies with the mains; real throughput is roughly half. Wi-Fi: an idle link drops to a low basic rate. Dashed: the hop's maximum. Before 2026-10-13 only the exporter's direct links exist (the LAN port speed, not the powerline rate).

panels.title: Sync rate (current)
panels.description: fritz_dsl_datarate_kbps{type="curr"}: what the line is synced at (your tariff profile). The real ceiling.

panels.title: Attainable rate
panels.description: fritz_dsl_datarate_kbps{type="max"} (same as fritz_wan_max_bitrate_bps): what the line could carry.

panels.title: Line capacity used
panels.description: Current sync rate as a share of the attainable rate. Well below 100 % means the tariff, not the line, limits the speed.

panels.title: CRC errors, 24 h
panels.description: Uncorrectable errors (fritz_dsl_crc_errors_count_total). They cost retransmissions; a few are normal.

panels.title: Sync rate history
panels.description: A change in the current rate means the line resynced.

panels.title: DSL errors per minute
panels.description: FEC errors are corrected and harmless in large numbers. CRC errors are lost data.

panels.title: Line attenuation
panels.description: Signal loss on the copper line. Lower is better; it depends on the distance to the street cabinet.

panels.title: Noise margin (SNR)
panels.description: Headroom against interference. Above ~6 dB is stable; drops point to interference or resyncs.

panels.title: WAN connections
panels.description: fritz_wan_connection_status and _uptime per connection and IP stack. internet2 is the LTE fallback, voip the telephony connection.

panels.title: IPv6 prefix
panels.description: Delegated IPv6 prefix from the provider (fritz_wan_ipv6_prefix_info).

panels.title: Provider management server (TR-069)
panels.description: The provider's auto-configuration server the FRITZ!Box reports to (fritz_tr069_acs_info).

panels.title: Remote management
panels.description: TR-069 and USP: whether the provider or MyFRITZ! can manage the box remotely.

panels.title: Inform interval
panels.description: How often the FRITZ!Box contacts the provider's TR-069 server.

panels.title: CPU temperature
panels.description: From fritz-extras (our add-on, fritz-extras/fritz_extras.py), which reads the FRITZ!Box web UI every 2 min. 60-80 °C is normal for a FRITZ!Box.

panels.title: CPU load
panels.description: From fritz-extras (our add-on, fritz-extras/fritz_extras.py), which reads the FRITZ!Box web UI every 2 min.

panels.title: RAM in use
panels.description: From fritz-extras (our add-on, fritz-extras/fritz_extras.py), which reads the FRITZ!Box web UI every 2 min. Fixed (system) + dynamic memory.

panels.title: Devices online
panels.description: From the FRITZ!Box network list, every 5 min (fritz-extras).

panels.title: fritz-extras
panels.description: Whether the add-on's last fetch worked. Errors: docker compose logs fritz-extras

panels.title: CPU temperature and load
panels.description: From fritz-extras (our add-on, fritz-extras/fritz_extras.py), which reads the FRITZ!Box web UI every 2 min.

panels.title: RAM
panels.description: From fritz-extras (our add-on, fritz-extras/fritz_extras.py), which reads the FRITZ!Box web UI every 2 min.

panels.title: Energy use per component
panels.description: Current energy use of each part, in percent of that part's maximum (the FRITZ!Box shows no watts). From the web UI page System → Energy Monitor.

panels.title: LAN traffic
panels.description: Your FRITZ!Box reports 0 for this counter (FRITZ!OS doesn't fill it on this model).

panels.title: LAN packets
panels.description: Your FRITZ!Box reports 0 for this counter (FRITZ!OS doesn't fill it on this model).

panels.title: Wi-Fi packets
panels.description: Your FRITZ!Box reports 0 for this counter (FRITZ!OS doesn't fill it on this model).

panels.title: FRITZ!Box scrape duration
panels.description: How long one read-out of the FRITZ!Box takes. The Prometheus timeout is 30 s.

panels.title: fritz-extras fetch duration
panels.description: How long the add-on's last fetch took: hosts = device list (every 5 min), system = web UI values (every 2 min).

panels.title: fritz-extras last success
panels.description: Seconds since the last successful fetch per source. Values older than 3 intervals are dropped.
